perception.plainEnglish: One look serves both the quiet glimpse and the sudden noise. Begin Play starts that look on a short loop. A creak or a bottle can start the same look immediately.
perception.whyGame: A second brain for sound will set a flag the stalk never reads, so the hunter ignores the bottle you just threw.

expansions.title: A closed door
expansions.detail: The channel stops on the door. The hunter does not see through it.

expansions.title: A bottle
expansions.detail: The bottle calls the same look right away. It does not wait for the next loop.

expansions.title: A miss
expansions.detail: A miss leaves the alert flag alone. Darkness is not a special case.

quiz.prompt: A creak, a bottle, and a sprint all need to alert the hunter. What do they call?
choices: The same Sense event the glimpse timer already uses
A private audio brain with its own alert float
quiz.why: One float, so the stalk cannot disagree with itself.

quiz.prompt: The line Alert = 1.f sits inside the hit branch of Sense. When does that line run?
choices: Only after the trace reports bHit
Every time the 0.2 second timer fires, hit or not
When the player opens the pause menu
When the save file is written
quiz.why: The assignment is gated on the hit.

quiz.prompt: Begin Play has just run on the hunter. Which node should be next?
choices: A looping timer at 0.2 seconds that calls Sense
A per-frame trace that never stops
AddToSlot for the key in the player's hand
quiz.why: The timer is the glimpse. Begin Play starts it once.

quiz.prompt: You give the creak its own AI component so audio feels special. What goes wrong?
choices: The stalk still reads the original alert flag and ignores the creak
Fuel cans can no longer stack
The limp animation plays on the hunter
quiz.why: The stalk was taught one flag.

quiz.prompt: A player throws a bottle while the hunter is mid-loop. What should happen before the next timer tick?
choices: The bottle calls Sense immediately and can set the alert flag
The bottle waits silently for the next 0.2 second look
The bottle yaws the nearest door
The bottle writes the player's limb health
quiz.why: Sound is the startle. It does not wait for the glimpse.

quiz.prompt: A missed horror trace should leave the alert flag unchanged.
quiz.why: The sample assigns only on a hit.

quiz.prompt: A closed door stands between the hunter and the player. What does the trace do?
choices: It continues through the door mesh
It sets the alert flag to 1 anyway
It opens the door with PlayFromStart
quiz.why: The channel is blocked by the door.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence matches the 0.2 second timer?
choices: It is the quiet glimpse, not the sound
It is the creak that plays with the door swing
It is the fear pulse that shakes the camera
It is the patrol step between route points
quiz.why: The timer glimpses. The sound startles.

quiz.prompt: Each co-op client runs Sense and the hunters disagree about the player. Who should trace?
choices: The machine that owns the hunter
Every client, then average the bools
Only the player who threw the bottle
The client with the lowest ping
quiz.why: One owner traces. Clients do not vote.

quiz.prompt: You want the alert flag to fade after a miss. Where does that write belong?
choices: On the else of the hit branch inside Sense
At the top of Tick, before the trace
Inside the save struct every frame
quiz.why: Decay is the miss path of the same event.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does one look serve both a quiet glimpse and a sudden noise?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What does the hunter ignore if sound sets a flag the stalk never reads?

interaction.plainEnglish: A fuse, a door, and a hide lever answer the same Interact call. The press traces a short way from the camera and calls that function on whatever it hits.
interaction.whyGame: A cast for every new prop means the next switch the art team adds never works until a programmer edits the trace.

expansions.title: A fuse
expansions.detail: The fuse implements Interact. The trace does not know the fuse class.

expansions.title: A hide lever
expansions.detail: The lever is the same function. It is not a second trace on Tick.

expansions.title: A miss
expansions.detail: Nothing in reach logs and returns. It does not alert the hunter.

quiz.prompt: A fuse, a door, and a hide lever all need to respond to use. What do they share?
choices: An Interact function the trace calls with ProcessEvent
A cast chain, one class per prop
A private Tick graph for each mesh
quiz.why: One call. The prop implements it.

quiz.prompt: The interact excerpt calls ProcessEvent on Interact after a hit. What does that line do?
choices: It runs the hit actor's own use function
It sets the hunter alert flag to 1
It adds one to the item stack count
It yaws the door hinge by the frame time
quiz.why: ProcessEvent is the interface call.

quiz.prompt: The use trace hit a hide lever. Which node comes next?
choices: A cast to the lever class, then a custom pin
PlayFromStart on a timeline the lever does not own
quiz.why: The lever implements the same function.

quiz.prompt: The miss branch of the use trace sets the hunter's alert flag. What goes wrong?
choices: Waving the crosshair at empty air alerts the hunter
The 0.2 second glimpse timer is destroyed
quiz.why: A miss only logs. Alert belongs to Sense.

quiz.prompt: The crosshair sits on a hide lever in a dark room. Where should the trace start?
choices: At the camera, along the crosshair
At the last saved door hinge
quiz.why: The player aims with the camera.

quiz.prompt: A missed use trace logs the miss and does not set the hunter alert flag.
quiz.why: The miss logs and returns.

quiz.prompt: Art adds a new wall switch. What has to be true for the existing use trace to operate it?
choices: The trace gains a new cast to the switch class
Begin Play registers the switch mesh by name
The switch writes the alert flag itself
quiz.why: The trace never lists classes.

quiz.prompt: Hide was given its own Tick graph so the prompt feels instant. What should the lever do instead?
choices: Implement Interact and wait for the use trace
Trace from the lever toward the player every frame
quiz.why: The lever is a prop, not a second look.

quiz.prompt: The generated line starts the trace at the owner's location plus a short forward vector. In this horror camera, what is wrong with that origin?
choices: The crosshair is on the camera
Forward vectors are illegal in a trace
The owner location is always the hunter
A forward vector replicates the door bool
quiz.why: Match the crosshair. The sample origin is the pawn.

quiz.prompt: Which line is the use function, not the hunter look?
choices: ProcessEvent on Interact after the use trace hits
GoingRight = true on the patrol path
quiz.why: Interact is the press. Sense is the look.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why do a fuse, a door, and a hide lever share one Interact call from a short camera trace?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What never works when art adds a switch and the trace still casts to the old props?

stalk.plainEnglish: The hunter walks a route on a one-second timer. When the alert flag is set, it leaves that route for a chase. When the flag fades, it goes back to the route.
stalk.whyGame: Chasing from Tick means the hunter keeps running through a pause and through a save load.

expansions.title: The way back
expansions.detail: The return path is still empty in the sample. Fill it or the hunter never walks home.

expansions.title: One look
expansions.detail: The stalk reads the flag. It does not trace again.

expansions.title: The timer
expansions.detail: Begin Play already started the route timer. AdvancePatrol must not start another.

quiz.prompt: The alert flag becomes 1 while the hunter is walking the route. What should happen?
choices: The hunter leaves the route for a chase event
The hunter keeps walking and ignores the flag
The hunter traces from its own eyes on Tick
The hunter opens the nearest door
quiz.why: The flag is the chase condition.

quiz.prompt: AdvancePatrol sets GoingRight = true on the A path. What did that line just decide?
choices: The hunter is walking toward the end of the route
quiz.why: GoingRight is the route direction.

quiz.prompt: The hunter should step along the route about once a second. Which node does that?
choices: AdvancePatrol on the timer Begin Play already started
A frame-by-frame step so the motion looks smooth
quiz.why: The route is a timer, not a frame.

quiz.prompt: AdvancePatrol starts a new timer every time it is called. What goes wrong?
choices: Timers pile up and the hunter sprints the route
quiz.why: Begin Play already owns that timer.

quiz.prompt: The B path has no points, and the hunter reaches the end of the route. What does the player see?
choices: The hunter stops, because the walk back was never authored
The hunter chases even though the alert flag is 0
The save slot clears the limb health
quiz.why: The return walk is the missing path.

quiz.prompt: The stalk reads the alert flag and should not run a second line trace.
quiz.why: Two traces pick different corners.

quiz.prompt: Sense misses and the alert flag decays. Which node should the hunter return to?
choices: A chase that ignores the decay
Playing the door from the start
Adding the item into a slot
quiz.why: Decay means back on the route.

quiz.prompt: The broken stalk chases from Tick. Which float should start the chase instead?
quiz.why: The chase reads Alert.

quiz.prompt: The game pauses while the hunter is chasing from Tick. What keeps moving?
choices: The hunter, because Tick still steps during the pause unless you gate it
No actor keeps moving, since a pause freezes the whole game
quiz.why: A chase event can be stopped. A raw Tick step is easy to forget.

quiz.prompt: You load a save and the hunter is already mid-chase from a Tick step. What was stored wrong?
choices: The chase was a frame step
The camera shake binding was saved
The door curve keys were saved
quiz.why: Save the flag. Let the chase event read it after load.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does the one-second route step yield to a chase only while the alert flag is set?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What keeps running through a pause if the chase is driven from Tick?

door.plainEnglish: The door swings on a timeline. Overlap starts the play. A flip-flop writes whether it is open. The creak plays with the swing and calls Sense.
door.whyGame: Yawing the hinge every frame never fires a finished event, so the creak either loops or never starts.

expansions.title: Co-op
expansions.detail: Replicate the open bool. Each machine plays the curve locally from that bool.

expansions.title: The creak
expansions.detail: The sound calls Sense. That is how a door alerts the hunter.

expansions.title: Load
expansions.detail: Set the curve to the end. Do not play it from the start or the creak fires again.

quiz.prompt: A player walks into the door volume. What starts the swing?
choices: PlayFromStart on the timeline built in the excerpt
Adding the frame time to the hinge yaw
quiz.why: Overlap plays the timeline.

quiz.prompt: FlipFlop writes IsOpen. What does that line record?
choices: Whether this swing is opening or closing
Whether the hunter can see the player
How much fear the player has
How many keys are in the inventory
quiz.why: IsOpen is the door, not the hunter.

quiz.prompt: The swing reaches the end of the curve. Which pin should play the creak's finished logic?
choices: The frame after the hinge stops turning
quiz.why: Finished is the end of the curve.

quiz.prompt: Tick yaws the hinge a few degrees per frame. What never happens?
choices: A finished event, so the creak has no clean start or stop
The bool existing on the actor
quiz.why: A yaw loop has no finished pin.

quiz.prompt: In co-op the hinge itself replicates and bandwidth spikes while the door moves. What should replicate instead?
choices: The open bool, with each machine playing the curve locally
Every bone of the door mesh
quiz.why: The bool is the state. The curve is local.

quiz.prompt: Loading an open horror door should set the curve to the open end.
quiz.why: PlayFromStart replays the creak into Sense.

quiz.prompt: The creak plays during the swing. What should that sound call?
choices: Sense, so the hunter can hear the door
The fear pulse, so a cupboard scares the player
The inventory add, so the door counts as a key
quiz.why: The creak is the audio path into the alert flag.

quiz.prompt: OnRep of IsOpen arrives on a client and the door is open. What should that client do?
choices: Set the curve to the open end without replaying the creak if the swing already finished
Call PlayFromStart every time the bool replicates. That replays the creak on proxies.
Trace from the door toward the hunter
quiz.why: The bool says where the door is. It is not a request to swing again.

quiz.prompt: Two timelines are fighting on one door. Who built the extra one?
choices: A second construction, often from load or from Tick, beside the excerpt's single component
The fear dispatcher. A cupboard creak is not what built the second timeline.
quiz.why: The excerpt builds one timeline.

quiz.prompt: A loaded house plays the creak and the alert flag climbs. How was the open bool applied?
choices: By setting the curve to the end in silence
By writing only the hunter mesh
quiz.why: Replay the swing and you replay the sound.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does overlap play the timeline, a flip-flop record open, and the creak call Sense?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What never starts if the hinge yaws every frame and no finished event fires?

limbs.plainEnglish: A bite is applied on the server. The write sits inside the authority check, and the result is clamped. Other machines hear the change and play the limp. They do not subtract again.
limbs.whyGame: A client that punches the screen early will snap back when the server's number arrives, and a second subtract on the notify makes the bite land twice.

expansions.title: The floor
expansions.detail: A bruise stops at 10 percent of that limb's max. Crossing zero is the downed state.

expansions.title: The notify
expansions.detail: OnRep plays the limp. It does not apply the bite.

expansions.title: The attacker
expansions.detail: The hunter calls Any Damage on the server.

quiz.prompt: A co-op bite should change limb health. Where does that write sit?
choices: Inside HasAuthority, reached from Any Damage on the server
On the owning client, so the screen punch is instant
Beside the limp in the notify
Beside the alert flag in the look
quiz.why: The server owns the number.

quiz.prompt: The excerpt assigns Health = 90.f inside the authority check. What is that number standing in for?
choices: A clamped result you still have to write
The final rule, and 90 is always correct
quiz.why: 90 is a sample. Replace it with the clamp.

quiz.prompt: The server has written the new limb value. Which node should run on the other machines?
choices: Another subtract of the same bite
quiz.why: The notify shows the result.

quiz.prompt: OnRep both limps and subtracts. What does the bitten player see?
quiz.why: The subtract already happened on the server.

quiz.prompt: A bruise would empty a limb whose max is 70. What floor was skipped?
choices: Ten percent of 70, so the limb stays at 7 until a real down
The number zero as the only legal value
quiz.why: A bruise does not down the limb.

quiz.prompt: The limp notify plays the result and does not subtract the bite again.
quiz.why: OnRep only presents the value.

quiz.prompt: The hunter attacks. Who calls Any Damage?
choices: The server copy of the hunter
quiz.why: Damage is a server event.

quiz.prompt: A medkit writes the limb on the owning client. What snaps when the server answers?
choices: The limb value, back to whatever the server still has
The camera's field of view permanently
quiz.why: The client number was never the authority.

quiz.prompt: Crossing zero on a limb is different from a bruise. What state is the zero cross?
quiz.why: The floor holds a bruise. Zero is down.

quiz.prompt: Which line is the co-op limb write, not the local beginner clamp?
choices: A subtract on Tick with no authority check
Clearing a stack on an empty overlap
quiz.why: Authority is what the second machine adds.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why is a co-op bite applied on the server, inside the authority check, and then clamped?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What snaps back, and what injures the pawn twice, if the client writes the limb and OnRep subtracts again?

inventory.plainEnglish: Keys and fuel cans use one slot path. Overlap adds the item when the stack count is positive. The most that stack can hold lives on the item, next to its name.
inventory.whyGame: A highlight on a key that fills the fuel can means the use trace is doing the pickup's job.

expansions.title: A key
expansions.detail: A key stack is usually one. The door asks the inventory if you have it.

expansions.title: Fuel
expansions.detail: Fuel may stack. The cap is on the asset.

expansions.title: The highlight
expansions.detail: The use trace can show a prompt. It does not increment the count.

quiz.prompt: A key and a fuel can both need to enter the inventory. What call should they share?
choices: A cast to the fuel-can class
Playing the door from the start
quiz.why: One slot path.

quiz.prompt: The overlap excerpt sees StackCount > 0.f and calls ProcessEvent on AddToSlot. What does that line do?
choices: It asks the inventory to take the item
quiz.why: Positive count means add.

quiz.prompt: The count is positive on overlap. Which node comes next?
quiz.why: The branch's true pin adds.

quiz.prompt: The use trace increments StackCount when the crosshair rests on a key. What goes wrong?
choices: Looking at the key fills the inventory without a pickup
quiz.why: The look highlights. Overlap adds.

quiz.prompt: A locked door should check for a key. Who asks?
choices: The door, calling into the inventory
quiz.why: Interact on the door asks the inventory.

quiz.prompt: The stack cap belongs as a magic number inside the overlap graph.
quiz.why: The cap sits on the item asset.

quiz.prompt: Fuel can stack and a key usually cannot. Where is that difference stored?
choices: On the item asset, beside the name
quiz.why: The asset owns the cap.

quiz.prompt: A highlight on a key fills the fuel can. Which event should have called AddToSlot?
choices: The overlap, when the count is positive
quiz.why: Overlap is the pickup.

quiz.prompt: The overlap runs and StackCount is 0. What does the excerpt do?
choices: It writes the count back to 0 and does not add
quiz.why: Empty means no add.

quiz.prompt: Fuel and a key share a cast to the can class. What breaks when a third item arrives?
choices: The timeline curve loses its keys
quiz.why: The cast list is why both should call AddToSlot.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why do keys and fuel share one slot path whose maximum lives on the item?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What job did the use trace steal if highlighting a key fills the fuel can?

fear.plainEnglish: Fear is an effect. Begin Play binds the listeners and starts a one-second timer. That timer calls ApplyEffect, which broadcasts. The camera and the UI listen. They do not poll the alert flag.
fear.whyGame: Shaking the camera from Tick keeps shaking for a frame after the flag fades, and it shakes during a pause.

expansions.title: The cupboard
expansions.detail: A door creak should call Sense, not the fear broadcast.

expansions.title: The pulse
expansions.detail: ApplyEffect is the broadcast. It is not the glimpse timer.

expansions.title: The save
expansions.detail: Save the fear float if it should resume. Do not save the delegate bindings.

quiz.prompt: The camera shake and the fear UI both need to react. What do they bind to?
choices: Polling each frame while the alert flag is high
quiz.why: Listeners bind. They do not poll.

quiz.prompt: ApplyEffect broadcasts OnEffect. What does that line do?
choices: It tells every bound listener that fear just pulsed
It sets the alert flag to 1
quiz.why: The broadcast is the pulse.

quiz.prompt: Begin Play runs on the fear component. What should it start?
choices: A one-second timer that calls ApplyEffect
A line trace from the camera
quiz.why: The excerpt starts that timer.

quiz.prompt: The camera shakes on Tick after the alert flag has already decayed. Why is there a leftover shake?
choices: Tick does not know the pulse ended
The door finished delegate shook the camera
The save slot replayed the creak
quiz.why: A broadcast ends cleanly. A Tick poll does not.

quiz.prompt: Every door creak broadcasts OnEffect and the player panics at a cupboard. What should the creak call?
quiz.why: The creak is a sound. Fear is a separate effect.

quiz.prompt: Fear delegate bindings belong in the save slot.
quiz.why: Bindings are rebuilt. The float may be saved.

quiz.prompt: Fear pulses on every 0.2 second glimpse. Where was the broadcast placed?
choices: Inside Sense, on the glimpse timer
On the fear pulse and its own one-second timer
Inside the door finished pin only
quiz.why: The glimpse is not the fear pulse.

quiz.prompt: Which node should the UI bind, rather than reading the alert flag itself?
quiz.why: The UI is a listener.

quiz.prompt: The game pauses and the camera is still shaking from Tick. What should have been pulsing instead?
quiz.why: A timer you own can pause. A Tick shake is easy to leave running.

quiz.prompt: The stalk has kept the alert flag at 1. What may the stalk apply?
choices: How much fuel an item holds
quiz.why: Fear is what a sustained alert can apply.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does Begin Play start one timer that calls ApplyEffect, instead of shaking the camera from Tick?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What keeps shaking after the flag fades if the camera shake lives on Tick?

save.plainEnglish: The night save stores the alert flag, the limb, whether the door is open, the patrol direction, the stack count, and the fear float if the pulse should resume. It does not store curves, bindings, or meshes.
save.whyGame: Playing the door from the start on load creaks, calls Sense, and wakes a house you just loaded as calm.

expansions.title: The curve
expansions.detail: Set the door curve to the end that matches the bool.

expansions.title: Order
expansions.detail: Apply doors before Sense starts, or the hunter glimpses a door that is not there yet.

expansions.title: When
expansions.detail: Write the struct on a finished event. Load it at Begin Play.

quiz.prompt: Which set belongs in the horror save struct?
choices: Alert, the limb, IsOpen, GoingRight, the stack count, and the fear float
The timeline curve keys and the delegate bindings
The hunter mesh and the door mesh
The raw key code for the use action

quiz.prompt: The sample assigns SlotValue = 1.f on Begin Play. What should replace that stand-in?
choices: The night struct, loaded at Begin Play
A second alert float for audio

quiz.prompt: The door bool loaded as open. Which step applies it without a creak?

Playing the timeline from the start

quiz.prompt: Sense starts before the loaded doors apply. What does the hunter gain?

quiz.prompt: The hunter mesh belongs in the night save.

quiz.prompt: GoingRight loaded and the alert flag did not. What chase is wrong?
choices: A chase that continues even though the loaded flag says the route
A door that opens because the route direction is true
A fuel can that stacks because the hunter faces right
A limp that plays because the route flipped

quiz.prompt: When should the horror struct be written?

quiz.prompt: When should that struct be loaded?
choices: At Begin Play, before Sense starts looking
On the first Tick after a chase

quiz.prompt: You pack the timeline curve into the slot to be safe. What are you actually saving?
choices: Playback machinery the bool already describes
quiz.why: The bool is enough. The curve is rebuilt.
